headline: Is Each Department's Scope Written Clearly — Including What You Don't Do?

headline: Can Every Patient See Your Service List Without Asking Anyone?

gaps.title: LIST IN A DRAWER

gaps.title: OUTDATED BOARD

gaps.title: ENGLISH ONLY
gaps.body: Display is not understandable for the local patient population.

gaps.title: HIDDEN LOCATION
gaps.body: Board is behind a pillar or only inside admin areas.

steps: Print the approved clinical and diagnostic service list for public display.
Place it permanently where patients and visitors can read it without asking.

headline: Is Registration and Admission Running on Written Guidance — Or Habit?
oe_text: The organisation uses written guidance for registering and admitting patients, including unidentified patients, covering out-patients, day-care, in-patients and emergency patients.

requirements.title: Written guidance exists
requirements.body: Written guidance covers registering and admitting patients, including unidentified patients.

requirements.title: All care settings
requirements.body: Guidance addresses out-patients, day-care, in-patients and emergency patients.

requirements.title: Patients are informed
requirements.body: Patients and families are informed of salient registration and admission steps.

gaps.title: NO WRITTEN SOP
gaps.body: Staff train new joiners from memory instead of an approved SOP.

gaps.title: EMERGENCY LEFT OUT
gaps.body: Guidance covers OPD only; emergency and unidentified patients are missing.

gaps.title: CONSENT NOT EXPLAINED
gaps.body: General consent scope is never explained at registration.

gaps.title: INCONSISTENT PRACTICE
gaps.body: Each shift registers patients differently.

steps: Approve one registration and admission SOP covering OP, daycare, IP, emergency and unidentified patients.
Train registration and casualty teams on the SOP this week.
Spot-check five registrations against the SOP and close gaps.

headline: Do Patients Get One Unique ID That Follows Them Everywhere?
oe_text: A unique identification number is generated at the end of registration, and visit numbers if used are linked back to that unique number.

requirements.title: Unique ID generated
requirements.body: A unique identification number is generated at the end of registration.

requirements.title: Visit numbers linked
requirements.body: Visit numbers, if used, are linked back to that unique number.

requirements.title: Same ID across records
requirements.body: The unique ID follows the patient across OP slips, files and reports.

gaps.title: DUPLICATE UHIDS
gaps.body: The same patient receives multiple unique IDs over time.

gaps.title: VISIT NOT LINKED
gaps.body: Visit numbers are not mapped to the master unique ID.

gaps.title: MANUAL GAPS
gaps.body: IDs are handwritten and recreated at each department.

gaps.title: NO LOOKUP
gaps.body: Staff cannot retrieve prior visits using the unique ID.

steps: Confirm your registration system always issues one master unique ID.
Link every visit number to that master ID and test retrieval.
Audit last week’s registrations for duplicate IDs and fix the process.

headline: Are You Accepting Patients You Cannot Actually Treat?

requirements.title: Match services to capacity
requirements.body: Patients are accepted only if the organisation can provide the required service.

requirements.title: Staff know the list
requirements.body: Registration and admission staff know the services the organisation provides.

gaps.body: Patients outside scope are admitted without a referral plan.

gaps.title: STAFF UNSURE
gaps.body: Registration cannot say which specialties are in scope.

gaps.title: NO REFERRAL PATH

gaps.title: EMERGENCY CONFUSION

Role-play three scenarios with registration this week.

gaps.title: UNKNOWN REDIRECTS
